units.translation: For in vain – the vision, passing through my hands, has gone.
being greatly mocked by enemies instead of friends, not ambiguously, in vain.
The toil is in vain.
Words leap high, dying in vain.
They sleep; in vain I utter things unfulfilled.
I seem to be lamenting in vain, alive, at a tomb.
Scaliger restored μάτην (it should have been μάταν). In M it is ἄτην, with an alpha written above.
I who have suffered many things, and in vain.
And some wretched person consoles me in vain from afar. ματροκασιγνήτα [mother's sister]. ματρόπολις [mother-city]. See under μητρ–.

The other form ἀμαυρόω is more common, which is read in Pers. 223 τάμπαλιν δὲ τῶνδε γαίας κάτοχ᾽ ἀμαυροῦσθαι σκότῳ [but the opposite of these things, held down by the earth, to be dimmed in darkness], where Blomfield wrote κάτοχα μαυροῦσθαι [held down, to be dimmed], a form which the tragedians do not seem to have used except when the meter required it.
Though he is mighty, nevertheless we dim him.
A torch still strong and not yet dimmed.

Corruptly in Suppl. 811 λύσιμα μάχιμα δ᾽ ἔπιδε, πάτερ [look upon the releasing, warlike things, father], where Weil conjectured λύσιμά μ᾽ ἄχειμ᾽ ἔπιδε, πάτερ [look upon me, releasing, stormless, father], which the scholiast seems to have read, who explained it by ἀτάραχα [untroubled]. The chorus had called itself ἀχείματον [stormless] at line 136.

When someone said μάχλον ἄμπελον [a flowing vine], meaning τὴν ῥεομένην [the flowing one], comedy called μάχλον [fierce] the one who is moist from inclination.
